A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Scaling Diffusion Language Models via Adaptation from Autoregressive Models. All 28 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original training and evaluation of DiffuGPT and DiffuLLaMA, including benchmark results, ablations, inference measurements, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical experiments and revises three reported benchmark scores in Table 1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same diffusion objective, attention-mask annealing, shift operation, time-embedding-free architecture, and sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluated tasks are unchanged. This includes the main language, reasoning, and infilling benchmarks and Appendix C's CD4 and controlled CodeLLaMA infilling experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main experiments and appendices, including GPT2, LLaMA2, SEDD, Plaid1B, and MD4 where originally evaluated. The newly cited Sahoo et al. work is not added as an experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1-4.2 and Appendix B retain the same training and evaluation settings. Lambada still uses exact-match accuracy, oracle word-token length, and the stated generation procedure; no protocol revision accompanies its changed scores.

E4.justification: The adaptation ablations, sampling sensitivity, self-correction example, global-planning analysis, controlled infilling comparison, continual-pretraining control, and decoding-speed analyses are unchanged, including Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. There are no changes to repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance testing, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially lowers Lambada accuracy for DiffuGPT-S from 45.0% to 21.6%, DiffuGPT-M from 60.5% to 30.3%, and DiffuLLaMA from 70.9% to 53.9%. Each changes from outperforming to underperforming its unchanged AR base: 25.9%, 37.7%, and 68.8%, respectively. This reverses the task-level comparison across all three proposed models under unchanged documented settings. Other results, including appendix results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, diffusion transitions, objectives, AR connection, and Appendix A derivations are unchanged, including Equations 1-25.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting 127M-7B AR models, competitiveness, diffusion capabilities, and released resources. The Lambada revisions do not produce corresponding claim revisions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications in Sections 4.3-4.5 and Appendix C are unchanged, including training-data limitations and the infilling comparison caveat. No explanation or new qualification addresses the revised Lambada results.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical data-processing, tokenizer, optimization, hardware, hyperparameter, and evaluation details. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Sahoo et al. (2024), Simple and Effective Masked Diffusion Language Models, to the discussion of discrete diffusion developments and adds its bibliography entry. The broader research positioning and novelty statements remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Jiawei Han's affiliation superscript and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Apart from the citation insertion, the prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference causes limited bibliography reflow across pages 16-18. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and placements. Table 1's numerical edits leave its existing underlines unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added citation improves attribution, but the substantial Lambada revisions are unexplained. Table 1 retains underlines meaning 'surpasses the base model' even though all three revised scores are now below their bases. The PDFs do not establish whether the numerical revisions correct earlier errors, so a possible accuracy benefit cannot be weighed reliably against the newly inconsistent presentation.
